_comment: PRD section 2's performance budgets. Rule R-E: budgets are laws — a gate is
never edited to make a build pass. ADR-018 clause 4: the absolute budget
changes only by ADR, with measured floor provenance.
IDLE RAM HAS TWO NAMES ON PURPOSE (ADR-017). They are different numbers and
conflating them turned a 116 MiB problem into a 300 MiB one:
The PRD 1.5 metric. GPU-rendered, on the 10.2 low-end row. The only
number a release claim may cite.
The per-PR tripwire, on the llvmpipe VM CI can actually run. COMPUTED
from the two fields, and deliberately never written down anywhere as a
number of its own, so the CI gate cannot move without editing the
offset's provenance and saying what was re-measured. A test enforces
AND TWO KINDS OF GATE (ADR-018 clause 3). The absolute budget is slack enough
not to be a coin flip, which makes it slack enough to hide steady creep. So
the blocking gate is absolute and the SENSITIVE one is relative: summed
userspace PSS against a rolling baseline. They catch different failures and

why: ADR-018 clause 1. ADR-017 fixed what is measured and left how often
undefined, so one run with ~50 MiB of noise decided a gate with under
4 MiB of headroom — a coin flip in both directions. Three runs, median,
and ALL THREE VALUES RECORDED so a marginal build reads as marginal
instead of as whichever number happened to land.

product.conditions: median of 3 runs, 2-minute settle each, 4 GB, GPU-rendered (ADR-017 §1, ADR-018 §1)
product.canonical_seat: PRD 10.2 low-end row: 4 GB RAM, integrated GPU
product.interim_source: the owner's GPU-accelerated local VM (MERIDIAN_VM_GL=1, virgl), until that machine exists

floor_provenance.basis: ADR-018 clause 2: measured post-trim floor plus one observed noise-spread of headroom
floor_provenance.note: The previous 1126 gate predated any GPU-measured evidence — a proxy carried forward, not a floor anyone had observed.

product.aspiration_note: 950 was the pre-evidence target. ADR-018 clause 2 reclassifies it as an aspiration contingent on the clause 5 investigation (Xwayland on-demand, kded module audit, KRunner preload). It gates NOTHING. If the investigation finds nothing, revise it by ADR rather than leave it standing as decoration.

render_offset.method: paired measurement, same post-trim image, both renderers: llvmpipe 1326.4 MiB minus GPU mean 1139.9 MiB (runs 1123.1, 1122.4, 1174.1)
render_offset.measured_by: WP-02, issue #32; adopted by ADR-018 clause 2
render_offset.supersedes: 182 MiB, measured 2026-09-03 pre-trim; drift +2.5%, inside ADR-017 clause 3's 25% threshold
render_offset.recalibrate: at every M-gate (ADR-017 clause 3); >25% drift is a finding, not an update

userspace_pss.baseline_source: median of the last 10 main-branch nightly runs (ADR-018 clause 3); the value here is the post-trim seed measured 2026-09-03
why: The creep detector. The absolute gate has ~60 MiB of slack by
construction, so it cannot see a build that gets steadily heavier. This
can. A PR over the delta fails until the increase is acknowledged in the
PR body with a reason — the first gate here that can be passed by
explaining rather than fixing, which is intentional, because creep is
sometimes bought deliberately. The acknowledgement is part of the record
and should say what was bought.

boot_seconds.conditions: cold boot, power-on to login screen, virtio SSD VM (PRD 2)
boot_seconds.note: Read from systemd's own firmware+loader+kernel+userspace total. Host-page-cache sensitive: the same image measured 16.9 s cold and 7.8 s warm, so a single over-gate reading on a busy host is not by itself a regression.
